mechanism: Calendar/seasonality. Long Japanese equities in January-June and short in July-December, following the published Dekansho-bushi effect.

literature.citation: Sakakibara, Yamasaki & Okada (2013), The Calendar Structure of the Japanese Stock Market: The 'Sell in May Effect' versus the 'Dekansho-bushi Effect', International Review of Finance 13(2):161-185.
literature.published_result: Mean Japanese stock returns are significantly positive in January-June and significantly negative in July-December; Nikkei 225 first-half cumulative performance greatly exceeded second-half performance.

phase0_public_postpublication.source: FRED NIKKEI225 daily close; economic source Nikkei Indexes
phase0_public_postpublication.reason: Use only full calendar years after the June 2013 publication; exclude incomplete September 2026.
phase0_public_postpublication.return_definition: Daily close-to-close simple return multiplied by the calendar-half position assigned to the return date.

costs.transition_rule: Costs apply only when the calendar-half position changes. A +1 to -1 or -1 to +1 reversal costs two one-way units.

phase0_public_postpublication.monthly_evaluation: Compound daily net returns into calendar-month observations after applying transition cost on the exact trading day of the half-year switch.
phase0_public_postpublication.subperiods: Four near-equal contiguous blocks by complete month count, frozen before price values are evaluated.

phase0_gates: 6-month moving-block bootstrap 95% lower mean monthly net return > 0
At least 3 of 4 fixed chronological subperiods have positive primary net cumulative return

promotion.true_ose_rule: Only if phase0 passes, preregister true OSE Mini confirmation with identical calendar sign and no season-boundary retuning.

forbidden: Use first-half long only or second-half short only after outcome
Switch to Sell-in-May months after outcome
Add trend, HAR, FX, BOJ or other filters to rescue failure
Use original 1950-2008 sample as validation evidence
next_action: Freeze monthly calendar/subperiod alignment from dates only, then run the post-publication public replication.
